paper_title: Nonfullerene Acceptor for Organic Solar Cells with Chlorination on Dithieno[3,2-b:2',3'-d]pyrrol Fused-Ring

knowledge_points.content: IPIC-4Cl is designed using an indacenobis(dithieno[3,2-b:2',3'-d]pyrrol) (INP) fused-ring core with branched 2-butyl-1-octyl (BO) side chains and chlorinated (dicyanomethylidene)-indan-1-one (IC) end groups.
knowledge_points.evidence: A narrow-band-gap molecular acceptor, IPIC-4Cl, featuring an indacenobis(dithieno[3,2-b:2',3'-d]pyrrol) (INP) core with 2-butyl-1-octyl side chains and chlorinated (dicyanomethylidene)-indan-1-one (IC) as electron-accepting end group, has been rationally designed...

knowledge_points.content: Binary organic solar cells based on PBDB-T:IPIC-4Cl achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 13.4% with a short-circuit current (JSC) of 22.2 mA cm⁻², an open-circuit voltage (VOC) of 813 mV, and a fill factor (FF) of 74.0%.
knowledge_points.evidence: Consequently, the OSCs constructed by PBDB-T:IPIC-4Cl obtain a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 13.4% with an extremely low energy loss of 0.51 eV... increased to 13.4% with a significantly enhanced Jsc value of 22.2 mA cm-2 and FF of 74.0% and Voc of 813 mV.

knowledge_points.content: The energy loss (Eloss) for the PBDB-T:IPIC-4Cl device is 0.51 eV, which is lower than most representative chlorinated NFAs reported in literature.
knowledge_points.evidence: More encouragingly, the Eloss value obtained from the IPIC-4Cl-based device decreased to 0.51 eV, which is lower than those for most of the representative chlorinated NFAs in the literature.

knowledge_points.content: Chlorination of the end groups in IPIC-4Cl results in a narrower optical bandgap (1.32 eV) compared to the fluorinated (1.38 eV) and non-halogenated (1.44 eV) counterparts.
knowledge_points.evidence: Moreover, the Eg opt calculated from the absorption onset for IPIC-4Cl was 1.32 eV, while 1.38 and 1.44 eV were calculated for IPIC-4F and IPIC, respectively.

knowledge_points.content: DFT calculations show that the chlorinated acceptor model (h-4Cl) possesses a larger dipole moment (11.82 D) than the fluorinated (11.04 D) and hydrogenated (8.47 D) models, indicating an enhanced intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) effect.
knowledge_points.evidence: The h-4Cl shows a larger dipole moment value (δ = 11.82 D) than h-4F (δ = 11.04 D) and h-4H (8.47 D), indicating the occurrence of an enhanced ICT effect in IPIC-Cl.

knowledge_points.content: The addition of 30 wt% PC71BM to the PBDB-T:IPIC-4Cl blend improves the PCE to 14.3% by acting as a phase mediator and electron-transporting channel, which enhances carrier generation and transport balance.
knowledge_points.evidence: Upon addition of PC71BM functioning as the phase mediator and electron-transporting channel into PBDB-T:IPIC-4Cl blend, the OSCs show an impressive PCE of 14.3%... the optimized PBDB-T:IPIC-4Cl:PC71BM (1:1:0.3, in weight ratio) device showed a maximum PCE of 14.3%...

knowledge_points.content: PBDB-T:IPIC-4Cl blend films exhibit higher and more balanced charge mobilities (μh = 1.26 × 10⁻⁴ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹, μe = 1.00 × 10⁻⁴ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹, μh/μe = 1.26) compared to IPIC-4F and IPIC blends.
knowledge_points.evidence: The PBDB-T:IPIC-4Cl blend films present higher and more balanced charge mobilities (μh = 1.26 × 10-4 cm2 V-1 s-1, μe = 1.00 × 10-4 cm2 V-1 s-1 and μh/μe = 1.26), in comparison with those of PBDB-T:IPIC-4F films... and PBDB-T:IPIC films...

knowledge_points.content: The chlorinated IPIC-4Cl neat film exhibits the strongest intermolecular aggregation with the smallest π-π stacking distance (dπ-π) of 3.45 Å, as determined by GIWAXS.
knowledge_points.evidence: The π-π stacking distance (dπ-π) was evaluated to quantize the crystallinity, and we found that IPIC-4Cl neat film has the smallest dπ-π of 3.45 Å. This indicates that IPIC-4Cl exhibits the strongest intermolecular aggregations...

knowledge_points.content: Trap-assisted recombination is suppressed in PBDB-T:IPIC-4Cl devices, indicated by a VOC versus light intensity slope of 1.16 kT/q, which is lower than that of IPIC-4F (1.21 kT/q) and IPIC (1.95 kT/q).
knowledge_points.evidence: the slope of IPIC-4Cl-based devices was decreased to 1.16 kT/q, slightly lower than that of PBDB-T:IPIC-4F blend film (1.21 kT/q) and significantly lower than that of IPIC-based devices (1.95 kT/q).

knowledge_points.content: Optimal device performance for IPIC series blends was achieved using chlorobenzene (CB) as the solvent, 0.5% (v/v) 1,8-diiodooctane (DIO) as an additive, and thermal annealing at 100 °C for 10 minutes.
knowledge_points.evidence: In detail, chlorobenzene (CB) was used as the processing solvent. In all three blend solutions (D:A = 1:1, in weight ratio), 0.5% (v/v) 1,8-diiodooctane (DIO) was added as processing additive. ...thermal annealing at 100 °C for 10 min is crucial...

knowledge_points.content: R-SoXS measurements revealed that the PBDB-T:IPIC-4Cl film possesses small domains, providing a high donor-acceptor (D:A) interface area for efficient exciton separation.
knowledge_points.evidence: Small domains in PBDB-T:IPIC-4Cl film indicated that more D:A interfaces are produced in blend film to efficiently facilitate exciton separation, which contributes to the high Jsc values for the binary devices.
